pages.title: Sorting and the 1G1R Election
pages.purpose: Document the sort-roms workflow: region/language/discard filtering, the parent-clone grouping and weighted election that picks one game per title, subfolder schemes, and how ROMfiles end up in the system directory, 1G1R and Trash — the workflow page several existing pages already link to but which does not exist.
instructions: Cover the real call chain in src/sort_roms.rs: main -> resolve_systems_by_name_like / prompt_for_systems -> per-system settings read -> sort_system -> sort_game -> the moves, plus sort_games_by_weight, compare_versions and trim_ignored_games as the election primitives.

Document the CLI-only knobs that override the database (--regions/--1g1r/--subfolders/--wanted/--all/--yes/--system) since MCP and GraphQL synthesize exactly these argv values — verify against src/mcp/write.rs sort_roms and src/mutation.rs.

Explain the settings each read consumes with system_id scoping (REGIONS_ALL, REGIONS_ONE, REGIONS_*_ARCADE, LANGUAGES, DISCARD_*, PREFER_PARENTS/REGIONS/VERSIONS/FLAGS, REGIONS_ONE_STRICT, REGIONS_*_SUBFOLDERS) and cross-link rather than duplicate the storage/scoping mechanics owned by /openwiki/architecture/settings-and-configuration.md.

Ground claims in the neighbouring tests under src/sort_roms/ (test_order_* and test_sort_1g1r_*) to pin ordering semantics; reference test files with correctly encoded relative links (spaces/parentheses as %20) so no broken-link marker is emitted.

State the on-disk outcome: system base directory, 1G1R subdirectory, Trash subdirectory, alpha subfolder scheme, and that Game.sorting/completion are the recorded result; note arcade systems bypass 1G1R and use REGIONS_*_ARCADE rom types instead, deferring merged-set detail to the arcade page.

Use a flowchart TD mermaid diagram for the per-parent-group election (group -> trim ignored -> region priority pick -> strict/completion gate -> destination), following the mermaid skill syntax rules: no semicolons, pipes, or bare unquoted parentheses in labels.
